nodes.content: Design a multi-tenant storage engine that isolates write latency while sharing compaction capacity and preserving crash-consistent tenant boundaries.
requirements: Keep tenant p99 write latency within 2× its standalone baseline during competing compactions within quotas.
Prevent cross-tenant data exposure and storage quota evasion across crashes and capacity reassignment.

nodes.content: Use per-tenant WALs and encryption keys, reserved foreground I/O, fair-share compaction, and atomic manifests binding extents to quota ownership.
How can compactions share I/O without pushing any in-quota tenant’s p99 write latency above 2× its standalone baseline?
Per-tenant foreground queues reserving 70% of device IOPS and weighted-deficit compaction keep in-quota write p99 ≤2× standalone.
Run TenantMix-8 with 70% foreground IOPS reservation and weighted-deficit compaction; compare tenant write p99 against standalone under competing compactions.
TenantMix-8: in-quota tenant B’s write p99 reached 2.7× standalone during competing compactions despite 70% foreground IOPS reservation.
Replace fixed IOPS reservation with latency-feedback compaction throttling because tenant B reached 2.7× standalone write p99.
Throttle compaction when 10-second tenant write p99 exceeds 1.5× standalone, then rerun TenantMix-8 to verify 2× bounds.
Implement 10-second per-tenant p99 feedback controlling compaction tokens, then rerun TenantMix-8 with competing compactions and enforced quotas.
CompactionController v1 adds 10-second tenant p99-triggered token throttling and TenantMix-8 output comparing write p99 against standalone.
Using CompactionController v1, rerun TenantMix-8 and compare tenant write p99 ratios and compaction throughput against fixed reservation.
TenantMix-8: CompactionController v1 held in-quota write p99 at ≤1.8× standalone while sustaining 82% of unthrottled compaction throughput.
Replacing fixed 70% IOPS reservation with 10-second p99 feedback and weighted-deficit compaction keeps bursty tenants’ write p99 ≤2× standalone.
Run TenantBurst-8 with 30-second write bursts and competing compactions on CompactionController v1; compare in-quota write p99 against standalone.
TenantBurst-8: under 30-second bursts and competing compactions, in-quota write p99 peaked at 1.9× standalone with CompactionController v1.
Adopt CompactionController v1: TenantMix-8 sustained 82% compaction throughput, while TenantBurst-8 kept in-quota write p99 ≤1.9× standalone.
TenantBurst-8 report records per-tenant write p99 ratios, burst schedules, compaction throughput, and controller token traces.
Pair atomic ownership manifests with epoch-fenced capacity leases, WAL-backed quota reservations, and per-extent key destruction before reuse.
Implement atomic manifests, fenced leases, and WAL-backed quota reservations; crash-test key destruction and reassignment for leakage and quota evasion.
Extend CompactionController v1 with WAL-backed quota reservations, atomic ownership manifests, and epoch-fenced leases; crash-test compaction-driven reassignment.
OwnershipManifest v1 records extent tenant, lease epoch, encryption-key ID, and WAL-backed reserved bytes in atomic commits.
If power fails during extent reassignment, how does recovery prevent stale-epoch reads and premature quota refunds?
Recovery fencing stale leases and withholding quota refunds until durable tombstones and key revocation prevents cross-tenant reads and undercount.
Run ReassignCrash-1000 against OwnershipManifest v1, injecting failures at lease fencing, tombstoning, and key revocation; audit reads and quota.
ReassignCrash-1000: 2/1,000 crashes let tenant A’s cached handles read B’s reassigned extents despite lease fencing and key revocation.
Reject OwnershipManifest v1 reassignment; require per-read epoch validation for cached handles because 2/1,000 crashes exposed reassigned extents.
Replay TenantBurst-8 report traces through OwnershipManifest v1 with crash-injected compaction reassignment; audit write p99, cross-tenant reads, and quota drift.
Crash-injected TenantBurst-8 had zero quota drift; ownership-manifest fsync raised in-quota write p99 to 2.3× standalone.
Add per-read epoch checks to OwnershipManifest v1; rerun ReassignCrash-1000 during reassignment, auditing unauthorized reads and quota refunds.
ReassignCrash-1000: per-read epoch checks stopped stale reads, but 3/1,000 crashes refunded 64 MiB before tombstone durability.
Retain epoch-checked reads; defer refunds until durable tombstones, batching non-boundary manifest fsyncs to address quota evasion and 2.3× p99.
Combine p99-feedback compaction, batched routine manifests, atomic ownership commits, epoch-checked reads, and durable-tombstone/key-revocation-gated refunds.
How can routine manifest batching keep write p99 ≤2× while crash-time reassignment preserves isolation and accurate quotas?
Batched routine manifests, synchronous ownership commits, epoch-checked reads, and post-tombstone/key-revocation refunds keep write p99 ≤2× without exposure or undercount.
Patch OwnershipManifest v1 with batched routine commits, synchronous ownership commits, epoch-checked reads, and tombstone/key-revocation-gated refunds; rerun TenantBurst-8 and ReassignCrash-1000.
TenantBurst-8: in-quota write p99 reached 2.2× standalone during ownership commits; ReassignCrash-1000 found no unauthorized reads or quota drift.
Dedicated metadata-device commits preserve tombstone/key-revocation-gated refunds and epoch-checked reads while keeping in-quota write p99 ≤2× standalone.
Route OwnershipManifest v1 commits to a dedicated metadata SSD; rerun TenantBurst-8 and ReassignCrash-1000, auditing p99, reads, and quota.
OwnershipManifest v2 places synchronous ownership commits on a dedicated metadata SSD and retains epoch-checked reads and tombstone-gated refunds.
TenantBurst-8 write p99 stayed ≤1.85× standalone; ReassignCrash-1000 found zero unauthorized reads or quota drift with metadata-SSD commits.
Integrate OwnershipManifest v2 with CompactionController v1; soak-test crashes and in-quota compactions for ≤2× standalone p99 and zero leakage/undercount.
Run 24-hour TenantSoak-8 integrating OwnershipManifest v2 and CompactionController v1; inject reassignment crashes, auditing write p99, unauthorized reads, and quota drift.
TenantSoak-8: frequent reassignments saturated the metadata SSD, raising in-quota write p99 to 2.3× standalone.
Retain metadata-SSD ownership commits, but throttle reassignment: TenantSoak-8 hit 2.3× write p99 versus TenantBurst-8’s 1.85×.
Gate reassignment on metadata-SSD utilization while retaining p99-feedback compaction, synchronous ownership commits, epoch-checked reads, and durable-refund barriers.
Gate reassignment above 70% metadata-SSD utilization; rerun TenantSoak-8 and ReassignCrash-1000 for ≤2× p99 and zero leakage/undercount.
Add 70%-utilization reassignment gate to OwnershipManifest v2, then run 24-hour TenantSoak-8 and ReassignCrash-1000 with quota audits.
OwnershipManifest v3 adds a 70%-metadata-SSD-utilization reassignment gate to v2’s synchronous ownership commits and epoch-checked reads.
Rerun TenantSoak-8 and ReassignCrash-1000 on OwnershipManifest v3; measure in-quota write p99, unauthorized reads, quota drift, and reassignment backlog.
TenantSoak-8: metadata commit bursts drove in-quota write p99 to 2.15× standalone despite gating; ReassignCrash-1000 showed zero leakage or drift.
How can reassignment avoid metadata commit bursts without weakening durable ownership boundaries or quota accounting?
A 200-commits/s token bucket with 20-token capacity should hold write p99 ≤2× while preserving synchronous ownership and quota barriers.
Add 200-commits/s, 20-token reassignment limiter to OwnershipManifest v3; rerun TenantSoak-8 and ReassignCrash-1000 against burst-related 2.15× p99.
TenantSoak-8 write p99 peaked at 1.92× standalone; ReassignCrash-1000 found zero unauthorized reads or quota drift with commit limiting.
Package OwnershipManifest v3 with commit limiting and CompactionController v1; validate sustained p99, reassignment backlog, isolation, and quota reconciliation.
Integrate OwnershipManifest v3’s 200-commits/s limiter with CompactionController v1; run crash-injected 72-hour TenantSoak-8, auditing backlog, p99, unauthorized reads, and quota.
OwnershipManifest v4 adds a 200-commits/s, 20-token reassignment limiter to v3’s metadata-utilization gate and durable ownership protocol.
Run crash-injected 72-hour TenantSoak-8 on OwnershipManifest v4; compare write p99, reassignment backlog, unauthorized reads, and quota drift.
72-hour TenantSoak-8: write p99 peaked at 1.94× standalone; reassignment backlog stayed ≤80 extents; zero unauthorized reads or quota drift.
Adopt OwnershipManifest v4 with CompactionController v1: commit limiting cut 2.15× p99 to 1.92–1.94× without exposure or quota drift.
